### a0028
--- stdout
--- stderr

The tag message has been left in .git/TAG_EDITMSG
ERROR: failed to create the signed tag. Check that your signing key is
       configured (git config user.signingkey; gpg.format matches your
       key type) and that its public key is in the trust root.

       Likely cause: user.signingkey ('ABCD1234EF') is not an SSH key or
       key file — it looks like a GPG key id from OpenPGP commit signing.
       Attestations are SSH-signed here (ssh trust root). Keep your GPG
       commit signing and set a key for attestations only:
             # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
             vetting_signing_key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
       (or switch git to SSH signing globally), or run 'sandbox vet'
       interactively and let it set this up for you.
--- log
--- meta
rc=1
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
--- usercfg
--- stat

### a0036

--- stderr

The tag message has been left in .git/TAG_EDITMSG
ERROR: failed to create the signed tag. Check that your signing key is
       configured (git config user.signingkey; gpg.format matches your
       key type) and that its public key is in the trust root.

       Likely cause: user.signingkey ('ABCD1234EF') is not an SSH key or
       key file — it looks like a GPG key id from OpenPGP commit signing.
       Attestations are SSH-signed here (ssh trust root). Keep your GPG
       commit signing and set a key for attestations only:
             # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
             vetting_signing_key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
       (or switch git to SSH signing globally), or run 'sandbox vet'
       interactively and let it set this up for you.

### a0638
--- tty

  git signing is not configured. Attestations are signed with your own SSH
  key — nothing is shared or fetched; verification uses public keys only.
  Configure git (globally) to sign with <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Configured: gpg.format=ssh, user.signingkey=<T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

  To be enrolled as a reviewer, your public key must be in the trust root.
  Your allowed_signers line (send it to your overlay maintainer, or append
  it to <T>/run/home/.sandbox/vetting/allowed_signers):

      t@example.invalid ssh-ed25519 <KEY>

--- log
--- meta
rc=0
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
[gpg]
	format = ssh
[user]
	signingkey = <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
--- usercfg
--- stat
644
### a0639
--- tty

  git signing is not configured. Attestations are signed with your own SSH
  key — nothing is shared or fetched; verification uses public keys only.
  Configure git (globally) to sign with <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Skipped. Configure it manually to attest — globally:
        git config --global gpg.format ssh
        git config --global user.signingkey <path-to-your-key.pub>
  or, to sign attestations only (leaving git config untouched):
        # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
        vetting_signing_key: <path-to-your-key.pub>
--- log
--- meta
rc=1
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
--- usercfg

  git signing is not configured. Attestations are signed with your own SSH
  key — nothing is shared or fetched; verification uses public keys only.
  Configure git (globally) to sign with <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_rsa.pub? [y/N]   Configured: gpg.format=ssh, user.signingkey=<T>/run/home/.ssh/id_rsa.pub

  To be enrolled as a reviewer, your public key must be in the trust root.
  Your allowed_signers line (send it to your overlay maintainer, or append
  it to <T>/run/home/.sandbox/vetting/allowed_signers):

      t@example.invalid ssh-rsa <KEY>

### a0710
--- tty

  Your git user.signingkey ('ABCD1234EF') is not an SSH key or key file — it
  looks like a GPG key id from OpenPGP commit signing. Attestations here are
  SSH-signed (the trust root is an allowed_signers file), and SSH signing
  reads user.signingkey as a key file path, so signing would fail with
  "Couldn't load public key ABCD1234EF".

  Your git config can stay exactly as it is: vetting_signing_key: in
  ~/.sandbox/config.yaml signs attestations (and only attestations) with an
  SSH key, while your commits keep their OpenPGP signature.
  Set vetting_signing_key: <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Configured: vetting_signing_key: <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (in <T>/run/uc.yaml);
  your git signing config was not changed.

  To be enrolled as a reviewer, your public key must be in the trust root.
  Your allowed_signers line (send it to your overlay maintainer, or append
  it to <T>/run/home/.sandbox/vetting/allowed_signers):

      t@example.invalid ssh-ed25519 <KEY>

--- log
--- meta
rc=0
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
--- usercfg
vetting_signing_key: <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
--- stat
600
### a0711
--- tty

  Your git user.signingkey ('ABCD1234EF') is not an SSH key or key file — it
  looks like a GPG key id from OpenPGP commit signing. Attestations here are
  SSH-signed (the trust root is an allowed_signers file), and SSH signing
  reads user.signingkey as a key file path, so signing would fail with
  "Couldn't load public key ABCD1234EF".

  Your git config can stay exactly as it is: vetting_signing_key: in
  ~/.sandbox/config.yaml signs attestations (and only attestations) with an
  SSH key, while your commits keep their OpenPGP signature.
  Set vetting_signing_key: <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Skipped. Either set it yourself:
        # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
        vetting_signing_key: <path-to-your-key.pub>
  or switch git to SSH signing (globally, or per-repo to leave your
  global commit signing alone):
        git config --global gpg.format ssh
        git config --global user.signingkey <path-to-your-key.pub>
--- log

rc=1

  reads user.signingkey as a key file path, so signing would fail with
  "Couldn't load public key ABCD1234EF".

  Your git config can stay exactly as it is: vetting_signing_key: in
  ~/.sandbox/config.yaml signs attestations (and only attestations) with an
  SSH key, while your commits keep their OpenPGP signature.
  Set vetting_signing_key: <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Skipped. Either set it yourself:
        # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
        vetting_signing_key: <path-to-your-key.pub>
  or switch git to SSH signing (globally, or per-repo to leave your
  global commit signing alone):
        git config --global gpg.format ssh
        git config --global user.signingkey <path-to-your-key.pub>

### a0854
--- tty

  git signing is not configured. Attestations are signed with your own SSH
  key — nothing is shared or fetched; verification uses public keys only.
  Configure git (globally) to sign with <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Configured: gpg.format=ssh, user.signingkey=<T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
--- log
--- meta
rc=0
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
[gpg]
	format = ssh
[user]
	signingkey = <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
--- usercfg
--- stat
644
### a0855
--- tty

  git signing is not configured. Attestations are signed with your own SSH
  key — nothing is shared or fetched; verification uses public keys only.
  Configure git (globally) to sign with <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub? [y/N]   Skipped. Configure it manually to attest — globally:
        git config --global gpg.format ssh
        git config --global user.signingkey <path-to-your-key.pub>
  or, to sign attestations only (leaving git config untouched):
        # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
        vetting_signing_key: <path-to-your-key.pub>
--- log
--- meta
rc=1
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
--- usercfg
--- stat
644

### a0863
--- tty

  git signing is not configured. Attestations are signed with your own SSH
  key — nothing is shared or fetched; verification uses public keys only.
  Configure git (globally) to sign with <T>/run/home/.ssh/id_rsa.pub? [y/N]   Skipped. Configure it manually to attest — globally:
        git config --global gpg.format ssh
        git config --global user.signingkey <path-to-your-key.pub>
  or, to sign attestations only (leaving git config untouched):
        # ~/.sandbox/config.yaml
        vetting_signing_key: <path-to-your-key.pub>
--- log
--- meta
rc=1
--- post
--- markers
--- gitconfig
--- usercfg
--- stat
644
